candidate.title: RARseq
candidate.scope: The RARseq row of the assigned Illumina poster: polyadenylated RNA → double-stranded cDNA → alternative MseI-only or MseI plus StyI-HF restriction digests → branch-specific adapter ligations → fragment libraries for transcript-derived SNP and polymorphic-locus discovery. RARseq means Restriction Site Associated RNA Sequencing. The adjacent Genome icon is explanatory target context, and the neighboring TL-seq, TATL-seq and TAIL-seq rows and nucleoside drawings are outside the assigned card. The two enzyme alternatives are retained within the single named RARseq assay. This is a schematic architecture, not a complete execution protocol.

states.label: Polyadenylated RNA representing expressed loci
features: The purple RNA carries a depicted AAAA(A)n tail and marked restriction-site positions; the chemical substrate for the subsequent restriction digest is its double-stranded cDNA copy.

The biological target is transcript-derived SNPs and polymorphic loci for population genomics. The nearby Genome icon is target context, with no material-transfer arrow from genomic DNA into this workflow.

operations.label: cDNA synthesis
operations.description: Convert the depicted RNA into double-stranded cDNA: an RNA sequence representation becomes a paired-strand DNA substrate for restriction digestion. This broad block covers first-strand reverse transcription and second-strand DNA synthesis.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper uses reverse transcriptase to generate the first strand and a DNA polymerase for the second strand. The source block is retained as a single schematic operation.
operations.information_effect: Preserves expressed transcript sequence in DNA. The library therefore samples transcribed loci rather than the entire genomic DNA sequence.

operations.label: Restriction digest
operations.description: In the upper alternative, cut double-stranded cDNA using MseI alone to produce restriction-defined cDNA fragments.
operations.mechanism: MseI is the single-digest restriction enzyme; the primary paper identifies it as a four-base cutter. No end repair or terminal phosphate changes are drawn.
operations.information_effect: Defines a restriction-associated subset of transcript-derived DNA fragments for this route; representation depends on the starting transcripts and suitable restriction sites.

operations.label: Restriction digest
operations.description: In the lower alternative, digest double-stranded cDNA with MseI and StyI-HF to produce a dual-enzyme restriction-fragment set.
operations.mechanism: The paper specifies the four-base cutter MseI and six-base cutter StyI-HF together. The lower caption is read as StyI-HF, resolving the small-font I/l ambiguity.
operations.information_effect: Defines a transcript-derived restriction-fragment repertoire using two enzymes. This is a separate local digestion instance, with no asserted equivalence or required merger with the single-digest route.

method_scopes.rationale: cDNA synthesis is shared preparation. MseI-only digestion connects exclusively to the upper ligation instance; MseI–StyI-HF digestion connects exclusively to the lower ligation instance. These are alternative RARseq preparations, not sequential digestion stages. Both are supported by the paper and the catalogue page whose heading and schematic match the target. The fan-out denotes available alternatives; it does not specify an aliquoting operation. The final shared Fragment library caption identifies the product class without establishing pooling. The primary paper also describes size selection, PCR enrichment, pooling, sequencing and analysis; those unshown execution steps are not inserted into the poster graph. The library readout is sequence variation in represented transcribed regions, not complete genome sequence. Expression-dependent starting material and restriction-fragment sampling limit which loci can be represented.
